scope: ephemeral two-host HTTPS writer-lease scope and injected-time rollback probe; not independent validation

counterexample.statement: After lease expiry denied sequence 2 at injected witness test time 150, moving the injected time source backward to 100 made the same lease valid again and sequence 2 was accepted.
counterexample.boundary: This changed an explicit test clock supplied through now_fn; it did not alter the physical witness OS clock. It demonstrates that the lease logic depends on rollback-resistant trustworthy time that is not presently established.

setup_notes: Port 4444 had no listener before the probe.
A narrow git fetch did not create the expected remote-tracking ref on neontic; checkout was corrected using an explicit fetch refspec before the service started.
An initial PowerShell Set-Content invocation created an untracked file named 100; it was deleted before service start and the test clock was then created using an explicit file write.
limitations: Both computers remain under the same operator and are not independent custody or independent validation.
Writer credentials remain bearer secrets configured directly on the witness service.
A compromised writer can cause fail-closed denial of service inside its authorized source/run/policy/sequence scope.
Expiry is not rollback-resistant because trustworthy monotonic time is not established.
Credential issuance, rotation, revocation, hardware binding and external identity governance are not established.
Witness-host compromise, durable storage rollback and availability loss remain outside the demonstrated protection.
This probe does not establish live containment, matched efficacy, comparator parity, scientific N, canonical efficacy or high assurance.
